Open items

Source: TODO.md

Maintainer notes: known issues and deferred work, carried forward from the package audit. Not installed with the package (.Rbuildignored).

Each item records why it was deferred, because in most cases the reason is that the change would alter reported numbers or produce a diff that is hard to review — not that the work is unclear.

Status at the time of writing: R CMD check gives 0 errors, 0 warnings and one NOTE (unable to verify current time, an artefact of the machine it was run on, not the package). Test suite: 114 assertions passing.

Statistical / numerical

1. mnTS() and mnGLMM() use different standard-error conventions

mnTS() fixes dispersion at its estimate and computes the Hessian over the remaining parameters, giving conditional standard errors (R/source_mnTS.R, the compute.information.matrix block). mnGLMM() computes the full Hessian including log-dispersion and inverts it, giving marginal standard errors (R/source_mnGLMM.R).

Inverting a submatrix of the Hessian and taking a submatrix of the inverse are not the same thing, so the two functions report standard errors that are not directly comparable when dispersion is estimated. When dispersion is fixed — the default — the question does not arise, because it is not a free parameter.

Deferred because aligning them changes reported standard errors for any model that estimates dispersion. Needs a decision on which convention is intended, ideally checked against the bootstrap (which is the recommended way to get standard errors anyway).

2. par["sigma"] can disagree in sign with sigma

sigma enters the likelihood squared, so the optimiser can settle on a negative value. The C++ applies abs() to the sigma field it returns but not to the sigma element of the par vector (src/source_mnTS_list.cpp, src/source_mnGLMM.cpp), so object$par["sigma"] and object$sigma can differ in sign.

The pure-R reference implementations in tests/testthat/helper-reference-impl.R do apply abs() there, so this is also a genuine divergence between the reference and the compiled code. The equivalency tests compare the likelihood and the B/mu/logLik outputs, not par, so it is not currently exercised.

summary() and coef() exclude sigma from their tables, so the practical impact is limited to anyone reading object$par directly.

Deferred because it is cosmetic in normal use, and changing the C++ output should come with a test that actually drives sigma negative.

3. mnGLMM() does not validate sigma.start

mnTS() rejects sigma.start < 0 with “Sigma is less than 0” (R/source_mnTS.R). mnGLMM() has no equivalent check even though it uses sigma the same way.

Deferred because adding a new stop() is a small behaviour change that was outside the scope of the round it was found in. Low risk to add.

4. Use inv_sympd for the symmetric positive-definite inversions

arma::inv(FF) in src/source_mnTS_list.cpp and arma::inv(S_sub) in src/source_mnGLMM.cpp both invert matrices that are symmetric and positive definite by construction. arma::inv_sympd is faster and more numerically stable.

Deferred because it is a different algorithm and would perturb results in the last few digits, which the equivalency tests assert to machine precision. Doing it means deciding on a tolerance for those tests.

5. Carry taxon and driver names through to every output matrix

Output matrices should carry the row and column names of the input data, so results can be read and plotted without relying on column order. Coverage is currently uneven. Verified on the Story Lake model:

Output Named?
mnTS: B0, B, C, V yes — taxa on both margins of C/V, covariates × taxa for B
mnTS: mu, y, se.y.fitted, se.mu.upper.fitted, se.mu.lower.fitted no — all Tmax × n and unnamed
mnGLMM: B, V, mu no
simulate()$Y, and therefore bootstrap() coefficient names no — becomes y1 … yn

Three separate pieces of work, in rough order of value:

(a) mnGLMM’s B, V and mu are unnamed — a regression from the C++ port. The pure-R mnGLMM.ml() set them (colnames(B) <- colnames(Y), rownames(B) <- colnames(X), and both margins of V) — that code still exists, but only in tests/testthat/helper-reference-impl.R, because the reference implementation is no longer what runs. Armadillo returns bare matrices, and mnGLMM() never re-applies the names, whereas mnTS() does exactly that after its own C++ call. So summary(glmm_mod) prints B and V with [,1] [,2] … headers. Fixing it means copying the pattern mnTS() already uses. Cheapest and clearest win of the three.

(b) mnTS()’s fitted-value matrices are unnamed. mu, y and the three se.* matrices are Tmax × n, so they want taxon column names. Row names are less obvious: the natural label is the time step, but the model iterates 1:max(Tsample) while the user thinks in ages or depths, which the package never sees. Column names alone would still be a clear improvement — anyone plotting fitted values currently has to trust column order.

(c) Bootstrap coefficients come back as y1 … yn. simulate.mnTS() builds Y.sim without column names, so refitting inside bootstrap.mnTS() triggers mnTS()’s fallback naming and every coefficient is labelled positionally. Both vignettes then hand-map y1 … yn back to taxa, which is fragile — the main vignette carries a callout-warning about it precisely because the packaged story_pollen_matrix has a different column order from the matrix the vignette builds, so the mapping is not transferable. The fix is to preserve colnames(mod$Y) on the simulated matrix. The vignette prose already promises this (“in future versions I will update the bootstrapping function to have the option of maintaining the species names”), so the note there should be updated at the same time.

Note when doing (c): it changes the row names of coef.table.boot, which is user-visible output. Worth a NEWS entry, and both vignettes’ relabelling code becomes unnecessary.

6. No guard on mu reaching 0 or 1

arma::pow(mu % (1 - mu), -1) (src/source_mnTS_list.cpp, src/source_mnGLMM.cpp) produces Inf if any fitted probability hits 0 or 1. The rcond check downstream catches the consequence and returns the 1e+10 guard value, so the optimiser recovers, but a direct check would give a clearer diagnostic.

Code quality

7. Run styler::style_pkg()

R/ mixes tab indentation (the original code) with spaces (the newer methods), sometimes inside a single function.

Deferred because a whole-package restyle produces a large whitespace-only diff. It should be its own commit, with nothing else in it, so that subsequent git blame and code review stay usable. Run it, commit it alone, then confirm the test suite and R CMD check are unchanged.

8. Vignette build cost

vignettes/multinomialTS-vignette.qmd takes about 30 minutes to render: it fits mnGLMM, two mnTS models, and a 5-replicate bootstrap at build time. That cost is paid on every R CMD build and every pkgdown deploy.

Options: reduce maxit.optim in the vignette, fit a smaller subset, or precompute the fits and ship them as internal objects. Note that shipping precomputed bootstrap output is what created the stale-data problem fixed in 1.1.0 — see data-raw/README.md — so any precomputation needs a regeneration script under data-raw/.

9. boot() deprecation shim

boot() forwards to bootstrap() with a deprecation warning (R/source_mnTS.R). Remove it in a future release, along with its man/boot.Rd and the Deprecated section of _pkgdown.yml.

Packaging / infrastructure

10. build.yml: validated for Windows and Apple Silicon, release job still untested

The binary-build workflow was substantially rewritten for 1.1.0 (pkgbuild::build() instead of devtools::build(), dependencies via setup-r-dependencies, a lipo architecture check, a tag guard on the release job).

A manual workflow_dispatch run confirmed the windows and macOS-arm64 legs build and upload artifacts correctly. The Intel leg has since been removed (see below).

Still unverified: the release job. It is guarded to tag pushes, so a manual dispatch never exercises it. The first v*.*.* tag push will be its first run. Failure is benign — needs: build means a failed build blocks publication entirely, so a partial release is not possible — but be ready to delete the tag and release and retry:

git push --delete origin v1.1.0 && git tag -d v1.1.0

Intel macOS: dropped, and why

macos-13 was the last free Intel runner and has been retired. Jobs requesting a retired label queue indefinitely rather than failing, which is what happened: the Intel leg sat “Waiting for a runner” for 18 hours.

The remaining Intel labels (macos-15-intel, macos-26-intel, macos-*-large) are larger runners, which GitHub bills even for public repositories — “Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public repositories or when you have quota available from your plan.” R packages with compiled code cannot be cross-compiled, so an Intel binary needs a native Intel machine.

The Intel leg was therefore removed rather than paid for. Reinstating it means either enabling billing and switching to macos-15-intel, or attaching a self-hosted Intel runner.

Worth noting this removed a broken asset, not a working one: before 1.1.0 both macOS legs ran on macos-latest, which has been Apple Silicon since early 2024, so every published macOS-x86_64 binary was really arm64.

11. Vignette re-building fails during R CMD check on Windows

R-CMD-check skips vignettes on the Windows job only (build_args includes --no-build-vignettes, args includes --ignore-vignettes). macOS and all three Linux jobs build them normally, and the pkgdown workflow renders both articles on every push, so rendering is still covered.

The Windows job failed about 3 minutes in — before any model fitting, which takes ~20 minutes — reporting “Vignette re-building failed” for both vignettes. The suspected cause is the quarto R package’s handling of system2(env = ) on Windows: it passes the environment assignment to the CLI as an argument, so quarto TMPDIR=C:\... -V errors with Unknown command "TMPDIR=...". That is reproducible locally with quarto R package 1.5.1 and CLI 1.7.30, though quarto::quarto_version() recovers from it and a direct quarto::quarto_render() succeeds — so the exact failure inside the vignette engine is not yet pinned down.

To diagnose properly the job log is needed (reading it requires admin rights on the repository). Worth re-testing after a quarto R package update before investing further.

12. Release checklist (recurring)

Not an open bug — a reminder, because the README pins version numbers. For each release:

  1. Bump Version: in DESCRIPTION and add a matching # multinomialTS x.y.z heading to NEWS.md. The heading must contain a parseable version — # multinomialTS (development version) makes R CMD check report “No news entries found”.
  2. Update the two binary install URLs in README.md to the new version. They 404 until the tag is pushed and build.yml publishes the assets.
  3. Push the tag; build.yml builds the binaries and publishes the release. Confirm both assets attached and that the URLs resolve.

Done for v1.1.0: assets published, both URLs verified returning HTTP 200.

13. Consider CRAN

The package now passes R CMD check --as-cran cleanly apart from the environmental time NOTE. If CRAN submission is ever the goal, the remaining work is a cran-comments.md, checking on r-hub/win-builder, and confirming the 30-minute vignette build is acceptable (it very likely is not — see item 8).
